reason: The reflector petals and receiver are the visible light-gathering and heating components of the furnace.
expectation: The petals and receiver should form the core of the solar furnace.

effect: The petals need steel rather than a direct connection to the receiver.
reaction: The required support makes sense, though the failed pairing was plausible.
reason: The compatibility list identifies steel as a partner for the reflector petals.
expectation: Steel should provide a support for the reflector petals.

effect: The reflector now has a rigid support, leaving the receiver as the likely next furnace component.
reaction: The braced ring gives the assembly a physically sensible shape.
reason: The supported reflector should direct sunlight toward the furnace receiver.
expectation: The receiver will attach to the reflector to form the solar furnace.

effect: The assembled furnace completes the first goal; preparing feedstock remains.
reaction: Focusing sunlight without fuel is a satisfying result.
reason: The screening mesh should separate finer material from the excavated regolith before forming it.
expectation: The mesh will produce screened regolith suitable for pressing.

effect: The mesh must first be combined with steel rather than used directly on the regolith.
reaction: A supported screen is plausible, though the direct screening attempt seemed reasonable.
reason: The compatibility feedback identifies steel as the mesh's available partner.
expectation: The steel will support the mesh to make a usable screen.

effect: The steel-supported mesh is now a regolith sieve, ready to screen the excavated material.
reaction: The rigid rim and collection tray make the extra preparation understandable.
reason: The sieve should separate the finer regolith needed for the formed feedstock.
expectation: The sieve will produce screened regolith for pressing.

effect: The screened regolith is ready for the forming step.
reaction: Separating the coarse stones makes the preparation clear.
reason: The workshop press is the visible equipment for forming the screened feedstock.
expectation: The press will form the screened regolith into feedstock.

effect: The press produced supported, unfired blanks and completed the feedstock goal; firing would be needed to bond the grains.
reaction: The distinction between shaping and finished strength was useful and satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Pressing the screened regolith was most worthwhile: it explained both how the blanks are formed and why they still need firing.

leastWorthwhile.text: The two failed direct combinations were somewhat repetitive, though the resulting support structures were plausible.

surprise.text: The blanks remain weak after pressing and need supported firing to bond their grains; forming them is not the same as finishing them.

arbitrary.text: Neither failed pairing felt entirely arbitrary, but needing to build a supported sieve before screening was not clear from the initial objects.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the blanks are fired and used, especially given the clear physical explanations so far.
